reconcile.note: Syriac word: the print has shin, then lamadh joined to a final alaph (the tall stroke on the left with the lamadh-alaph join), with one small vowel mark above. That matches Readings 2 and 3 (ܫܠܳܐ). Reading 1 (ܫܠܳ) leaves out the alaph, which is printed. Reading 3 adds a pthaha under the shin, but no mark is printed below the shin, so I left it out. The vowel above looks like zqapa (a small ring). It seems to sit over the lamadh, but in the lamadh-alaph join it is hard to tell which letter it belongs to. Last Hebrew word: the final letter sits on the baseline and does not drop below it. That makes it ה, not final ף, which in this type drops below the line, so it is שָׁלָה (Reading 1), not שָׁלַף (Readings 2 and 3). Under the lamed, the mark looks like qamets rather than patah. נָשַׁל: nun has qamets, shin has patah and the right-hand shin dot; all three readings agree. There is a comma after the Syriac word and after נָשַׁל, and a full stop at the end.

reconcile:v2:69bcb03a0b421080dde338c0f83.text: נְשֹׂא שָׁלָל 2 Chr. 14, 12. Contra, חִלֵּק שָׁלָל
reconcile:v2:69bcb03a0b421080dde338c0f83.note: Under the nun of the first word there is a vertical two-dot mark (sheva), not the qamets tick that Readings 2 and 3 have (נָשָׂא). Above the shin there is a sin dot on the left and a second dot to its left (holem), with no qamets tick beneath, so the shin reads שֹׂ. Together these give the infinitive form נְשֹׂא, which matches Reading 1. Reading 1 had two spaces after "12."; the printed gap there is a little wide but is one word space, so I wrote one space. The other words match all three readings: שָׁלָל has qamets ticks under the shin and the first lamed, and חִלֵּק has hiriq, a dagesh in the lamed and tsere. The small dots are faint at this scan size, so the holem in particular is a fairly confident reading rather than a certain one.

reconcile:v2:c7dea9f2a5808b5fe9953dd1af1.note: Syriac word: the print has shin, then lamadh joined to a final alaph (the tall stroke on the left with the lamadh-alaph join), with one small vowel mark above. That matches Readings 2 and 3 (ܫܠܳܐ). Reading 1 (ܫܠܳ) leaves out the alaph, which is printed. Reading 3 adds a pthaha under the shin, but no mark is printed below the shin, so I left it out. The vowel above looks like zqapa (a small ring). It seems to sit over the lamadh, but in the lamadh-alaph join it is hard to tell which letter it belongs to. Last Hebrew word: the final letter sits on the baseline and does not drop below it. That makes it ה, not final ף, which in this type drops below the line, so it is שָׁלָה (Reading 1), not שָׁלַף (Readings 2 and 3). Under the lamed, the mark looks like qamets rather than patah. נָשַׁל: nun has qamets, shin has patah and the right-hand shin dot; all three readings agree. There is a comma after the Syriac word and after נָשַׁל, and a full stop at the end.

reconcile:v2:bd476cc6c9f397c034524e3870d.note: The only difference is the vowel under the lamed of the second Hebrew word. Under that lamed, two dots sit side by side at the same height, which is tsere (ֵ). Patah would be a single horizontal bar, and none is printed. That matches Reading 1, שָׁלֵו, and rules out שָׁלַו in Readings 2 and 3. The rest of the line agrees with the print. Reading right to left, שָׁלָה comes first (qamets under shin and under lamed, shin dot on the right), then a comma, then שָׁלֵו (qamets under shin) and a full stop. 'Job 9, 4' has a space after the comma.

reconcile:v2:4538afd40d46abd4c1be6c70717.text: Sacy, Studer, read לְצַוָּארָיו שָׁלָל, a spoil
reconcile:v2:4538afd40d46abd4c1be6c70717.note: Word order: read right to left, the word with the sheva under its first lamed (right end of the Hebrew, next to the comma) is printed first, so לְצַוָּארָיו comes before שָׁלָל. Reading 1 reverses the order. Under the dageshed vav there is a single T-shaped stroke, the same shape as the qamets under the resh and under ש and ל in שָׁלָל. It is not two stacked dots, so it is qamets (as in Reading 3), not the sheva in Reading 2. Reading 2's sheva may be the familiar form from Judges 5:30 (לְצַוְּארֵי) supplied from memory. Also printed: sheva under the first lamed, patah under the tsade, and the shin dot. The comma is set tight against the Hebrew.

reconcile:v2:fb06931564cc32e0d5544798c93.note: The printed word is three letters: shin, then lamadh, then final mim (the angular final form at the left). No final alaph is printed, so Reading 2 (ܫܠܳܡܐ) is wrong on the letters, and its zqapha doesn't fit the mark either. There is one vowel mark, above the lamadh, so Reading 1 (no points) is missing it. The mark is a small peaked shape, like a caret with a tick at the top. I read it as the Western rbasa (ܶ), the sideways-epsilon shape, which gives šlem, the Peal form, as in Reading 3. It is not clearly the small upright alaph used for zqapha. The image is small, so I can't completely rule out another Western vowel sign, which is why confidence is only "likely". Spacing is plain: one space after "Syr." and one before "id."

reconcile:v2:e7e1e2d06fcd25c8c95bb60b45f.note: Reading 1 matches the print. The readings differ only on the second Hebrew word. Under the lamed of the pausal form there is a vertical stem hanging below the tsere dots, which is an atnach (U+0591). The page shows it because the form is in pause. Readings 2 and 3 leave this accent out. Everything else is the same in all three readings and matches the ink: hireq under the shin, tsere under the lamed, and shureq in the final vav. Piel is printed in small caps, written here as 'Piel'. 'to' is italic.

reconcile:v2:15ca8ce13f71978ac0e3e36ab46.note: The only difference between the readings is the vowel under the lamed of שלם. In the ink there is a single short horizontal stroke under the lamed, which is a patah. It is not two side-by-side dots, which would be a tsere. The same patah stroke appears under the lamed of שִׁלַּם in the next printed line. Readings 2 and 3 have the tsere of the usual dictionary piel form, which is not what is printed. 'thing,' is followed by a space and then 'as'.

reconcile:v2:7972f8f19028ca8b4af85f0fd98.note: The readings differ only in the vowel on the Syriac word. A small caret-shaped Western (Jacobite) vowel sign is clearly printed above the word, between the lamadh and the final mim. That rules out Reading 1, which has no vowel. Readings 2 and 3 encode this sign as rbasa (U+0736), giving šlem, the Peal form that fits "to consent". At this resolution the caret shape can't be firmly told apart from a Western zqapa (U+0733), so the identification is likely, not certain. Everything else matches all three readings: "Pu. no. 2.", a wide gap before "Syr.", unpointed ܠ after "c.", the comma tight against ܠ, and "to consent," at the end.
